translations.literal: Prince of Qi Wenxiang then went to Luo province.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Wenxiang then went to Luo province.

sentences.zh: 冬十月癸未，以開府儀同三司、咸陽王坦為太傅。

translations.literal: Tenth month of winter, on guiwei day, Tan, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies with open office and Prince of Xianyang, was made grand preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on guiwei day, Tan, equal in honor to the three excellencies with open office and prince of Xianyang, was made grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以開府儀同三司潘相樂為司空。

translations.literal: On jiawu day Pan Xiangle, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies with open office, was made minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day Pan Xiangle, equal in honor to the three excellencies with open office, was made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 十有二月甲辰，吳郡王蕭正表薨。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on jiachen day, Prince of Wu commandery Xiao Zhengbiao died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiachen day, Prince of Wu commandery Xiao Zhengbiao died.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以并州刺史彭樂為司徒。

translations.literal: On jiyou day Peng Yue, regional inspector of Bing province, was made minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day Peng Yue, regional inspector of Bing province, was made minister of education.

sentences.zh: 是歲，蠕蠕、地豆于、室韋、高麗、吐谷渾國並遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: That year Rouran, Dudouyu, Shiwei, Koguryo, and Tuyuhun all sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year Rouran, Dudouyu, Shiwei, Koguryo, and Tuyuhun all sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 八年春正月辛酉，帝為齊文襄王舉哀於東堂。

translations.literal: Spring, first month of the eighth year, on xinyou day, the emperor held mourning for Prince of Qi Wenxiang in the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the eighth year, on xinyou day, the emperor held mourning for Prince of Qi Wenxiang in the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，詔贈齊文襄王假黃鉞、使持節、相國、都督中外諸軍事、齊王璽綬，轀輬車、黃屋、左纛、前後部羽葆、鼓吹、輕車介士，備九錫之禮，諡曰文襄王。

translations.literal: On dingmao day an edict posthumously granted Prince of Qi Wenxiang the yellow battle-axe, commissioner with full powers, chancellor, commander of all military affairs within and without, the Qi prince's seal and sash, the imperial carriage with curved canopy, yellow roof, left banner, front and rear feathered parasols, drum and pipe music, light chariots and armored escorts, and the rites of the Nine Bestowals; his posthumous title was Prince Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day an edict posthumously granted Prince of Qi Wenxiang the yellow battle-axe, commissioner with full powers, chancellor, commander of all military affairs within and without, the Qi prince's seal and sash, the imperial carriage with curved canopy, yellow roof, left banner, front and rear feathered parasols, drum and pipe music, light chariots and armored escorts, and the rites of the nine bestowals; his posthumous title was Prince Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，詔齊王為使持節、丞相、都督中外諸軍事、錄尚書事、大行臺、齊郡王，食邑一萬戶。

translations.literal: On wuchen day an edict made the Prince of Qi commissioner with full powers, chancellor, commander of all military affairs within and without, recorder of Masters of Writing affairs, grand mobile office, and Prince of Qi commandery, with a fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day an edict made the prince of Qi commissioner with full powers, chancellor, commander of all military affairs within and without, recorder of Masters of Writing affairs, grand mobile office, and prince of Qi commandery, with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，地豆于、契丹國並遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: On jiaxu day Dudouyu and Khitan both sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day Dudouyu and Khitan both sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 二月甲申，葬齊文襄王，車駕祖於漳濱。

translations.literal: Second month, on jiashen day, Prince of Qi Wenxiang was buried; the imperial carriage farewelled him on the Zhang bank.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiashen day, Prince of Qi Wenxiang was buried; the imperial carriage farewelled him on the Zhang bank.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以尚書令高隆之為太保。

translations.literal: On gengyin day Gao Longzhi, director of the Masters of Writing, was made grand preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day Gao Longzhi, director of the Masters of Writing, was made grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 三月庚申，進齊郡王爵為齊王。

translations.literal: Third month, on gengshen day, the Prince of Qi commandery was advanced in rank to Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengshen day, the prince of Qi commandery was advanced in rank to prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 夏四月乙巳，蠕蠕遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Fourth month of summer, on yisi day, Rouran sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on yisi day, Rouran sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 五月甲寅，詔齊王為相國，總百揆，封冀州之勃海、長樂、安德、武邑，瀛州之河間、高陽、章武，定州之中山、常山、博陵十郡，二十萬戶，備九錫之禮；

translations.literal: Fifth month, on jiayin day, an edict made the Prince of Qi chancellor, overall director of the hundred affairs, with fief over ten commanderies of Ji, Ying, and Ding provinces totaling two hundred thousand households and the full rites of the Nine Bestowals;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jiayin day, an edict made the prince of Qi chancellor, overall director of the hundred affairs, with fief over ten Ji, Ying, and Ding commanderies totaling two hundred thousand households and the full rites of the nine bestowals;

sentences.zh: 以齊國太妃為王太后，王妃為王后。

translations.literal: the Qi state's grand consort was made queen mother and the princess consort was made queen.
translations.idiomatic: the Qi state's grand consort was made queen mother and the princess consort was made queen.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，詔歸帝位於齊國，即日遜於別宮。

translations.literal: On bingchen day an edict returned the imperial throne to the state of Qi; that same day he abdicated to a separate palace.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day an edict returned the imperial throne to the state of Qi; that same day he abdicated to a separate palace.

sentences.zh: 帝好文學，美容儀。

translations.literal: The emperor loved literature and had handsome bearing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved literature and had handsome bearing.

sentences.zh: 力能挾石師子以踰牆，射無不中。

translations.literal: His strength could lift stone lions over a wall; in shooting nothing missed.
translations.idiomatic: He could lift stone lions over a wall; in archery he never missed.

sentences.zh: 嘉辰宴會，多命羣臣賦詩，從容沉雅，有孝文風。

translations.literal: At festive gatherings on auspicious days he often ordered the ministers to compose poetry; easy and grave in manner, he had the manner of Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: At festive gatherings on auspicious days he often had ministers compose poetry; calm and grave in manner, he had something of Emperor Xiaowen's style.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄王嗣事，甚忌焉，以大將軍中兵參軍崔季舒為中書黃門侍郎，令監察動靜，小大皆令季舒知。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi Wenxiang succeeded to affairs he greatly resented this; he made Grand General Central Army Staff Member Cui Jishu a secretariat yellow gate attendant and ordered him to watch the emperor's movements; large and small all had to be known to Jishu.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Qi Wenxiang took power he deeply resented this; he made Cui Jishu, staff member of the grand general's central army, a secretariat yellow gate attendant to watch the emperor's every move, great and small alike.

sentences.zh: 文襄與季舒書曰：「癡人復何似？

translations.literal: Wenxiang wrote Jishu: "How does the fool compare now?
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang wrote Jishu: "How is the fool now?

sentences.zh: 癡勢小差未？

translations.literal: Has the fool's condition improved a little?"
translations.idiomatic: Has his condition improved a little?"

sentences.zh: 」帝嘗與獵於鄴東，馳逐如飛。

translations.literal: The emperor once hunted east of Ye, galloping in pursuit like flight.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once hunted east of Ye at a gallop.

sentences.zh: 監衞都督烏那羅受工伐從後呼帝曰：「天子莫走馬，大將軍怒。

translations.literal: Supervising Guard Commissioner Wunaluo Shougongfa called from behind: "Son of Heaven, do not gallop—the Grand General will be angry!"
translations.idiomatic: Guard commissioner Wunaluo Shougongfa called from behind: "Son of Heaven, do not gallop—the Grand General will be angry!"

sentences.zh: 」文襄嘗侍飲，大舉觴曰：「臣澄勸陛下酒。

translations.literal: Wenxiang once attended drinking, raised a great cup, and urged the emperor: "Your servant Cheng urges Your Majesty to drink."
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang once raised a great cup at drink and urged the emperor: "Your servant Cheng urges Your Majesty to drink."

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅，曰：「自古無不亡之國，朕亦何用此活！

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and said: "From antiquity there has been no state that did not perish—what use is this life to me!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and said: "From antiquity no state failed to perish—what use is this life to me!"

sentences.zh: 」文襄怒曰：「朕！

translations.literal: Wenxiang raged: "Imperial We!"
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang raged: "Imperial We!"

sentences.zh: 朕！

translations.literal: Imperial We!"
translations.idiomatic: Imperial We!"

sentences.zh: 狗脚朕！

translations.literal: Dog-foot imperial We!"
translations.idiomatic: Dog-foot imperial We!"

sentences.zh: 」文襄使季舒毆帝三拳，奮衣而出。

translations.literal: He had Jishu strike the emperor three blows with the fist and flung his robes and went out.
translations.idiomatic: He had Jishu strike the emperor three blows and stormed out.

sentences.zh: 明日，文襄使季舒勞帝，帝亦謝焉。

translations.idiomatic: The next day Wenxiang sent Jishu to console the emperor; the emperor also apologized.

translations.idiomatic: The emperor bound a hundred lengths and gave them to him, saying: "That too is only one length!"

sentences.zh: 帝不堪憂辱，詠謝靈運詩曰：「韓亡子房奮，秦帝魯連耻。

translations.literal: Unable to bear worry and insult, the emperor chanted Xie Lingyun's poem: "When Han perished Zifang rose; the Qin emperor was shamed before Lu Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to bear insult, the emperor chanted Xie Lingyun: "When Han perished Zifang rose; the Qin emperor was shamed before Lu Lian.

sentences.zh: 本自江海人，忠義動君子。

translations.idiomatic: Men of rivers and seas—loyalty and righteousness move gentlemen."

translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang led troops into the palace and said: "Your Majesty, what do you mean by rebelling!

translations.idiomatic: My father and I preserved the altars—how have we failed you!

translations.idiomatic: He was about to kill the consorts.

translations.idiomatic: I spare not even my own person—how much more consorts!"

translations.literal: Wenxiang left the couch, kowtowed, and wept loudly begging pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang left the couch, kowtowed, and wept for pardon.

sentences.zh: 於是酣飲，夜久乃出。

translations.literal: Then they drank heavily; only late at night did he go out.
translations.idiomatic: Then they drank heavily until late at night before he left.

sentences.zh: 居三日，幽帝於含章堂，大器、瑾等皆見烹於市。

translations.idiomatic: Three days later he imprisoned the emperor in the Hall of Blended Splendor; Daqi, Jin, and the others were all boiled alive in the market.

translations.idiomatic: When the throne was to be yielded to Prince Wenxuan, Xu of Xiangcheng, Pan Xiangle, minister of works, Zhang Liang, attendant-in-ordinary, Zhao Yanchen, yellow gate gentleman, and others asked to enter with reports.

sentences.zh: 帝在昭陽殿見之，旭曰：「五行遞運，有始有終。

translations.idiomatic: The emperor received them in Zhaoyang Hall. Xu said: "The Five Phases pass in turn; there is beginning and there is end.

sentences.zh: 齊王聖德欽明，萬姓歸仰。

translations.idiomatic: The prince of Qi's sacred virtue is revered and bright; the ten thousand regions turn to him.

translations.idiomatic: The emperor composed his face and said: "This matter has been deferred long; I shall respectfully yield and withdraw."

translations.idiomatic: It was at once given to Yang Yin, who presented it to the emperor—ten articles in all.

translations.idiomatic: Lady Li of Zhao recited Prince Si of Chen's poem: "My lord, cherish your jade body and together enjoy the years of gray hair."

translations.idiomatic: " From the queen downward all wept.

translations.idiomatic: The emperor elbowed him and said: "I fear Heaven and follow the people in yielding the throne to the chancellor—what low slave dares press a man!"

translations.idiomatic: " De still would not descend.

translations.idiomatic: When they went out through Cloud Dragon Gate the princes, dukes, and hundred officials in full dress bowed in farewell. The emperor said: "Today is no worse than the Duke of Changdao or Emperor Xian of Han."

translations.literal: " The crowd were all grief-stricken; Gao Longzhi wept freely.
translations.idiomatic: " The crowd were grief-stricken; Gao Longzhi wept freely.

translations.idiomatic: He then entered the northern city and lodged in Sima Ziru's southern residence.

translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wenxuan went on tour he always had the emperor accompany him.

translations.idiomatic: The empress was enfeoffed princess of Taiyuan and often tasted the emperor's food to guard and watch over him.

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 魏書卷十二 諸本目錄此卷注「闕」，百衲本、南本卷後附宋人校語云：「魏收書孝靜紀亡，後人補以北史，又取高氏小史、修文殿御覽附益之。

translations.literal: In the tables of contents of the various editions of Wei Shu, volume 12, this volume is marked "deficient"; after the Baina, Southern, and Bureau editions a Song scholar's collation note says: "Emperor Xiaojing's annals in Wei Shou's book are lost; later men supplemented them from the Northern History, and also added material from the Gaoshi Xiaoshi and the Xiowen Hall Imperial Overview."
translations.idiomatic: The tables of contents of the various Wei Shu editions mark this volume deficient; after the Baina, Southern, and Bureau editions a Song scholar's note says: "Emperor Xiaojing's annals in Wei Shou's book are lost; later men supplemented them from the Northern History and also added material from the Gaoshi Xiaoshi and the Xiowen Hall Imperial Overview."

sentences.zh: 」殿本刪取前二句入考證。

translations.literal: " The Palace edition deleted the first two sentences and placed them in textual notes.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace edition deleted the first two sentences and placed them in textual notes.

sentences.zh: 高似孫史略卷二云：「靜帝紀補以高氏小史。

translations.literal: Gao Sisun's Shilue, volume 2, says: "Emperor Jing's annals were supplemented from the Gaoshi Xiaoshi."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Sisun's Shilue, volume 2, says: "Emperor Jing's annals were supplemented from the Gaoshi Xiaoshi."

sentences.zh: 」今按此紀記事較北史為詳，如載詔書，記高歡父子事，記戰事等很多為北史所略，紀中稱高歡、高澄為「獻武王」、「文襄王」，稱高洋為「今上」、「齊王」，稱西魏及梁為「寶炬」、「蕭衍」，全同魏收書。

translations.literal: " Now on examination this annals records events in more detail than the Northern History—for example edicts, affairs of Gao Huan and his sons, and battles—much of which the Northern History omits; in the annals Gao Huan and Gao Cheng are called "Duke Xianwu" and "Prince Wenxiang," Gao Yang "the present sovereign" and "Prince of Qi," and Western Wei and Liang "Baoju" and "Xiao Yan," all exactly as in Wei Shou's book.
translations.idiomatic: On examination this annals is more detailed than the Northern History in edicts, the affairs of Gao Huan and his sons, battles, and much else the Northern History omits; it calls Gao Huan and Gao Cheng "Duke Xianwu" and "Prince Wenxiang," Gao Yang "the present sovereign" and "prince of Qi," and Western Wei and Liang "Baoju" and "Xiao Yan," all as in Wei Shou's book.

sentences.zh: 當取之源出魏書之高氏小史和修文殿御覽。

translations.literal: The sources must be the Gaoshi Xiaoshi and Xiowen Hall Imperial Overview that derive from Wei Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The sources must be the Gaoshi Xiaoshi and Xiowen Hall Imperial Overview that derive from Wei Shu.

sentences.zh: 唯紀末自「齊天保元年五月己未封帝為中山王」以下至終，全採北史，幾乎一字不易。

translations.literal: Only from "In the first year of Tianbao of Qi, fifth month, on jiwei day, the emperor was enfeoffed Prince of Zhongshan" to the end the text is wholly taken from the Northern History, almost word for word.
translations.idiomatic: Only from "In Qi Tianbao year 1, fifth month, jiwei day, the emperor was enfeoffed prince of Zhongshan" to the end the text is wholly taken from the Northern History, almost word for word.

sentences.zh: 這段歷記高澄對元善見孝靜帝的侮慢態度和元善見被迫讓位以及遇酖而死，魏收決不敢寫下來，北史乃取自北齊書高德政傳和他書。

translations.literal: That passage records Gao Cheng's insulting treatment of Yuan Shanjian Emperor Xiaojing, his forced abdication, and death by poison—what Wei Shou dared not write; the Northern History took it from the Northern Qi Shu biography of Gao Dezheng and other books.
translations.idiomatic: That passage records Gao Cheng's insults to Emperor Xiaojing Yuan Shanjian, his forced abdication, and death by poison—what Wei Shou dared not write; the Northern History took it from the Northern Qi Shu biography of Gao Dezheng and other books.

sentences.zh: 紀中有些記載也表示出於北史的痕跡。

translations.literal: Some entries in the annals also show traces of the Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: Some entries in the annals also show traces of the Northern History.

sentences.zh: 如天平二年「侯淵」訛「侯梁」，與北史同。

translations.literal: For example, in the second year of Tianping "Hou Yuan" is written erroneously as "Hou Liang," the same as the Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: For example, in Tianping year 2 "Hou Yuan" is written erroneously as "Hou Liang," the same as the Northern History.

sentences.zh: 北史避唐諱，改「淵」為「深」，才訛作「梁」。

translations.literal: The Northern History, avoiding Tang taboo, changed "Yuan" to "Shen" and then corrupted it to "Liang."
translations.idiomatic: The Northern History, avoiding Tang taboo, changed "Yuan" to "Shen" and then corrupted it to "Liang."

sentences.zh: 魏書本作「侯淵」，「淵」「梁」字形不相似，顯見是承北史訛文。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu original reads "Hou Yuan"; the graphs for "Yuan" and "Liang" are not similar—it is clearly a corruption inherited from the Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu originally reads "Hou Yuan"; "Yuan" and "Liang" are not similar graphs—it clearly inherits a Northern History corruption.

sentences.zh: 又如興和二年，見「西魏行臺宮永和」，魏書例稱西魏為「寶炬」，今忽稱「西魏」，也是採自北史之證。

translations.literal: Again, in the second year of Xinghe appears "Western Wei grand mobile office Gong Yonghe"; Wei Shu normally calls Western Wei "Baoju"—to call it "Western Wei" here is also proof of borrowing from the Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: Again, in Xinghe year 2 appears "Western Wei grand mobile office Gong Yonghe"; Wei Shu normally calls Western Wei "Baoju"—suddenly saying "Western Wei" is further proof of Northern History borrowing.

sentences.zh: 又卷九八蕭衍傳中記梁、魏戰事，天平以前，都與諸紀相符，而天平以後，却多為此紀所不載，知原文所有，小史本多刪削。

translations.literal: Again, in volume 98, the biography of Xiao Yan, Liang–Wei battles before Tianping all match the various annals, but after Tianping much is omitted in this annals—showing that what the original had was largely cut in the Xiaoshi version.
translations.idiomatic: In volume 98, Xiao Yan's biography, Liang–Wei battles before Tianping match the annals, but after Tianping much is absent here—showing the Xiaoshi version cut much of the original.

sentences.zh: 大抵此紀以高氏小史為主，參考修文殿御覽和北史，補上小史不載的一些事跡。

translations.literal: Broadly, this annals chiefly follows the Gaoshi Xiaoshi, with reference to the Xiowen Hall Imperial Overview and Northern History, supplementing deeds the Xiaoshi does not record.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly this annals chiefly follows the Gaoshi Xiaoshi, with reference to the Xiowen Hall Imperial Overview and Northern History, supplementing what the Xiaoshi omits.

sentences.zh: 儀同三司賀拔勝 按本書卷八０、周書卷一四賀拔勝傳，勝自梁還，即入西魏，大統十年

translations.literal: Equal in Protocol to the Three Dukes Heba Sheng. Comment: This book juan 80, Zhoushu juan 14, Biography of Heba Sheng, says after returning from Liang Sheng immediately entered Western Wei; in Datong year 10
translations.idiomatic: Heba Sheng, Equal in Protocol to the Three Dukes. Juan 80 of this book and Zhoushu juan 14 (Biography of Heba Sheng) relate that on returning from Liang he at once entered Western Wei and that in Datong year 10

sentences.zh: 〈五四四〉
死於關中，至本年已先死三年，且從未入東魏，豈得為東魏「討侯景」。

translations.literal: by this year had already died three years earlier, and never entered Eastern Wei—how could he be Eastern Wei's "campaign against Hou Jing."
translations.idiomatic: he had died in Guanzhong—three years before the present year—and never served Eastern Wei; he could not figure in an Eastern Wei "campaign against Hou Jing."

sentences.zh: 張森楷云：「『勝』疑是『仁』之訛。

translations.literal: Zhang Senkai states: "'Sheng' is suspected to be corruption of 'Ren.'"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Senkai proposed: "'Sheng' is probably a corruption of 'Ren.'"

sentences.zh: 」當是。

translations.literal: That is correct.
translations.idiomatic: That is surely right.

sentences.zh: 衍署景河南大將軍 御覽卷一０四

translations.literal: Yan appointed Jing Grand General of Henan. Yulan juan 104
translations.idiomatic: Yan appointed Jing Grand General of Henan. Yulan juan 104

sentences.zh: 〈五０二頁〉
「河南」下有「王」字。

translations.literal: below "Henan" has the character "prince."
translations.idiomatic: adds the character "prince" after "Henan."

sentences.zh: 按梁書卷三武帝紀三太清元年二月稱「以景為大將軍，封河南王」，與御覽合。

translations.literal: Comment: Liangshu juan 3, Annals of Emperor Wu part 3, second month of Taqing year 1 says "made Jing Grand General, enfeoffed as Prince of Henan," agreeing with Yulan.
translations.idiomatic: Liangshu juan 3 (Annals of Emperor Wu, part 3), second month of Taqing year 1, reads "Jing was made Grand General and enfeoffed as Prince of Henan," which matches Yulan.

sentences.zh: 「河南大將軍」無此軍號或官名。

translations.literal: "Grand General of Henan" is not such a military title or office name.
translations.idiomatic: There was no army designation or office called "Grand General of Henan."

sentences.zh: 雖梁書卷五六侯景傳也作「河南大將軍」，實不足據。

translations.literal: Although Liangshu juan 56, Biography of Hou Jing, also has "Grand General of Henan," it is really not to be relied on.
translations.idiomatic: Liangshu juan 56 (Biography of Hou Jing) likewise has "Grand General of Henan," but that reading is not authoritative.

sentences.zh: 「河南」下當脫「王」字。

translations.literal: Below "Henan" the character "prince" should be missing.
translations.idiomatic: The character "prince" has dropped after "Henan."

sentences.zh: 以汾州刺史賀仁為太保 按「賀」下當脫「拔」字。

translations.literal: Made Fenzhou Governor He Ren Grand Guardian. Comment: below "He" the character "Ba" should be missing.
translations.idiomatic: He Ren, governor of Fenzhou, was made Grand Guardian. The syllable "Ba" is missing after "He."

sentences.zh: 北齊書卷四文宣紀武定七年十二月記「太保賀拔仁為并州刺史」可證。

translations.literal: Beiqishu juan 4, Annals of Emperor Wenxuan, twelfth month of Wuding year 7 records "Grand Guardian Heba Ren as governor of Bing province" can verify.
translations.idiomatic: Beiqishu juan 4 (Annals of Emperor Wenxuan), twelfth month of Wuding year 7, records "Grand Guardian Heba Ren as governor of Bing province," which confirms it.

sentences.zh: 八月 卷一０五之四天象志補記是年「八月，淮南三王謀反誅」。

translations.literal: Eighth month. Juan 105-4, Monograph on Astral Omens, supplement, records that year "eighth month, the three princes of Huainan plotted rebellion and were executed."
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month. The Astral Omens monograph supplement in juan 105-4 notes for that year: "Eighth month: the three Huainan princes plotted rebellion and were put to death."

sentences.zh: 志所謂「徵應」，即採本紀記事附會，此事今本孝靜紀不載，當出魏收此紀原文。

translations.literal: The so-called "correlative response" in the monograph means adopting annal entries and forcing correspondence; this matter is not in the present Xiaojing annal but should come from Wei Shou's original annal text.
translations.idiomatic: The monograph's "correlative responses" lift annal entries and read them back as omens fulfilled; the episode is absent from the extant Xiaojing annal but should come from Wei Shou's original text of this annal.

sentences.zh: 通鑑卷一０六

translations.literal: Zizhi tongjian juan 106
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi tongjian juan 106

sentences.zh: 〈四九五九頁〉
本年八月記荀濟、元瑾等與「華山王大器、淮南王宣洪、濟北王徽等謀誅

translations.literal: This year's eighth month records Xun Ji, Yuan Jin and others with "Prince of Huashan Daqi, Prince of Huainan Xuanhong, Prince of Jibei Hui and others plotting to kill
translations.idiomatic: The eighth month of this year records Xun Ji, Yuan Jin, and others together with "Prince of Huashan Daqi, Prince of Huainan Xuanhong, Prince of Jibei Hui, and others plotting to kill

translations.literal: (Gao)
translations.idiomatic: (Gao)

translations.literal: Cheng."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng."

sentences.zh: 今此紀末採北史魏紀五，也載此事，但不舉淮南、濟北二王。

translations.literal: Now at the end of this annal adopting Beishi Wei annals part 5, also records this matter, but does not name the two princes of Huainan and Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: The closing section of this annal, drawn from Beishi (Wei annals, part 5), also reports the affair but does not name the Huainan and Jibei princes.

sentences.zh: 通鑑所本，直接、間接亦出於魏書此紀原文。

translations.literal: What Zizhi tongjian is based on, directly or indirectly, also comes from this Wei shu annal original text.
translations.idiomatic: The Tongjian account, whether directly or at one remove, likewise derives from this Wei shu annal.

sentences.zh: 淮南王宣洪附見卷六陽平王熙傳，乃熙五世孫，云：「武定中，與元瑾謀反誅」，與天象志、通鑑合。

translations.literal: Prince of Huainan Xuanhong appears in appendix in juan 6, Biography of Yangping Wang Xi, fifth-generation descendant of Xi, says: "mid Wuding, plotted rebellion with Yuan Jin and was executed," agreeing with Astral Omens monograph and Zizhi tongjian.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Huainan Xuanhong appears in juan 6 (Biography of Yangping Wang Xi) as Xi's fifth-generation descendant: "In mid-Wuding he plotted rebellion with Yuan Jin and was executed"—in agreement with the Astral Omens monograph and the Tongjian.

sentences.zh: 秋八月甲戌 按本年八月己丑朔，無「甲戌」。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, jiaxu. Comment: this year eighth month new moon on jichou, there is no "jiaxu."
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, eighth month, jiaxu. The eighth month of this year began on jichou; there was no jiaxu day.

sentences.zh: 北史卷五魏紀五「甲戌」系於四月，乃誤刪「秋八月」所致，不足據。

translations.literal: Beishi juan 5 Wei annals part 5 attaches "jiaxu" to fourth month, caused by wrongly deleting "autumn eighth month," not to be relied on.
translations.idiomatic: Beishi juan 5 (Wei annals, part 5) places jiaxu in the fourth month because "autumn, eighth month" was wrongly deleted and cannot be trusted.

sentences.zh: 當從北史卷六齊紀上作「八月庚寅」。

translations.literal: Should follow Beishi juan 6 Qi annals part 1 as "eighth month, gengyin."
translations.idiomatic: The date should follow Beishi juan 6 (Qi annals, part 1): "eighth month, gengyin."

sentences.zh: 蕭衍弟子北徐州刺史封山侯蕭正表以鍾離內屬 諸本「封山」作「中山」，御覽卷一０四

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's younger clansman, governor of North Xu province, Marquis of Fengshan Xiao Zhengbiao submitted Zhongli. In all editions "Fengshan" is written as "Zhongshan," Yulan juan 104
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhengbiao, a younger clansman of Xiao Yan, governor of North Xu province and Marquis of Fengshan, surrendered Zhongli. All editions write "Fengshan" as "Zhongshan." Yulan juan 104

sentences.zh: 〈五０三頁〉
、通鑑卷一六一

translations.literal: and Zizhi tongjian juan 161
translations.idiomatic: and Zizhi tongjian juan 161

sentences.zh: 〈四九九五頁〉
作「封山」。

translations.literal: has "Fengshan."
translations.idiomatic: read "Fengshan."

sentences.zh: 按梁書卷二二、南史卷五一臨川王宏傳附見正表，都說正表封的是「封山侯」。

translations.literal: Comment: Liangshu juan 22 and Nanshi juan 51, Biography of Linchuan Wang Hong, appendix on Zhengbiao, both say Zhengbiao was enfeoffed as "Marquis of Fengshan."
translations.idiomatic: Liangshu juan 22 and Nanshi juan 51 (Biography of Linchuan Wang Hong, appendix on Zhengbiao) both give his title as Marquis of Fengshan.

sentences.zh: 梁書卷五六侯景傳亦見「北徐州刺史、封山侯正表」。

translations.literal: Liangshu juan 56, Biography of Hou Jing, also has "governor of North Xu province, Marquis of Fengshan Zhengbiao."
translations.idiomatic: Liangshu juan 56 (Biography of Hou Jing) likewise has "governor of North Xu province, Marquis of Fengshan Zhengbiao."

sentences.zh: 列侯封邑，例取縣名，中山是郡，且非梁地。

translations.literal: For ranked marquises enfeoffment fief normally takes county name; Zhongshan is a commandery, and not Liang territory.
translations.idiomatic: Marquisates normally take a county name as fief; Zhongshan is a commandery and not Liang territory.

sentences.zh: 封山縣屬交州新昌郡，見南齊書卷一四州郡志。

translations.literal: Fengshan county belonged to Xinchang commandery, Jiao province; see Nanqishu juan 14, Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Fengshan county lay in Xinchang commandery, Jiao province (Nanqishu juan 14, Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies).

sentences.zh: 「中」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: Character "zhong" is erroneous; now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: "Zhong" is erroneous and is emended accordingly.
